subject: Hosted→Dedicated transfer credit allocation & throughput design
messages:
From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: samantha.ortiz@picoai.com
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted→Dedicated transfer credit allocation & throughput design

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for walking through PicoAI's production goals. Per our conversation today I pulled together a concrete proposal to move you from Hosted usage to a Dedicated GPU pool with a short bridge so you don't lose momentum during the initial commit period. Key constraints you mentioned:

- Steady-state throughput target: ~275–325 tokens/sec (across inference fleet) for prompt-heavy inference.
- Latency SLO target: p95 < 130ms for 512-token context on gpus we recommend.
- Minimal operational downtime during cutover; need at least 2 weeks of overlap.

Proposal highlights (attached spreadsheet has pricing math):

1) Commit structure: 12‑month reserved commit for a 6-GPU pool (A100 equivalent), with a quarterly true-up.
2) Conversion credits: We propose a one-time conversion credit equal to 2 months of average hosted spend (applied to first invoice).
3) Bridge months: To smooth the transition, Redwood will provide 3 bridge months where billed committed units are offset by a 40% credit; this tapers to full commit billing after month 3.
4) Throughput guarantee: We will guarantee a baseline throughput of 250 tokens/sec per pool under the committed SLA. If we miss the SLA due to platform issues, you get pro-rata credits.
5) Add‑ons: optional 24/7 support and an SRE onboarding week (one-time) to help with traffic shaping and batching.

Questions for you: does a 3‑month taper look feasible operationally, or would you prefer a longer taper at a lower credit percentage? Also, are there any procurement constraints on how credits are recognized on your side (PO timing, invoice netting)?

I've attached the rate sheet and a sample ramp plan. Neha and Marissa are looped to confirm technical sizing and finalize the SOW.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.com
[Attachment: Hosted-to-Dedicated_Rates_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: samantha.ortiz@picoai.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: eng_ops@picoai.com, legal@picoai.com
Date: Wed, 08 Sep 2027 17:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated transfer credit allocation & throughput design

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Quick answers and a few clarifying questions from our side:

- The projected throughput matches our internal numbers for steady traffic; however we expect a 2x burst pattern for short windows during model retrains. Can you confirm burst capacity behavior (auto-burst or queued)?
- Procurement asks that credits be applied on invoices rather than as an ARR reduction. Can the conversion credit be represented as a line-item credit over the first 2 invoices?
- Bridge months: 3 months at 40% helps, but given our fiscal quarter cutover we were hoping for a longer taper that covers the quarter boundary — would Redwood consider 5 bridge months at 25%?
- Legal wants to make sure the throughput guarantee has a clear measurement window and exclusion list for customer-driven degradations (e.g., sudden batch-size changes).

If you can send an updated sheet that shows both the 3x40% and 5x25% scenarios side-by-side, that would help speed approval. Also we can do a quick technical sync with Marissa's team next week.

—Samantha
Head of Platform | PicoAI
[Attachment: PicoAI_ramp_plan_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 09 Sep 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Hosted→Dedicated transfer credit allocation & throughput design

Looping Rishi for pricing/legal framing and Marissa for sizing confirmation. Customer asked for two scenarios (3 months @ 40% vs 5 months @ 25%) and invoice-line credit treatment. Points to resolve internally before we send a formal revision:

- Financial impact: Rishi, can you run net-present-value on both scenarios? We should include the impact to committed AR and show ARR recognition timing differences if credits are applied via invoice vs ARR contra.
- Sizing: Marissa, confirm whether 6 GPUs at the configuration Priyom suggested cover the 2x burst for short windows or whether we should propose a small burst buffer (1–2 hot GPUs behind autoscale). Need your call on whether burst capacity is auto-provisioned (best-effort) or should be contractually available as part of the commit.
- SLA language: Rishi/Legal, customer wants explicit measurement windows. We should propose 30-day rolling measurement with exclusions for customer-driven batch anomalies.

Let's try to get a recommended option by EOD Friday so we can get the revised sheet to Samantha before their procurement review next week.

Neha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha...@redwood.com

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 16:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted→Dedicated transfer credit allocation & throughput design

Summary and recommended approach (internal) —

After running the numbers and sizing notes from Marissa, my recommendation to present to PicoAI:

1) Pricing scenarios (both presented in the updated attachment):
   - Option A (faster taper): 3 bridge months at 40% credit. Upside: quicker revenue recognition, simpler accounting for Redwood. Downside: smaller help across quarter boundary for the customer.
   - Option B (quarter-friendly taper): 5 bridge months at 25% credit. Upside: aligns to customer's fiscal timing, better customer retention signal. Downside: delays some revenue recognition and increases short-term credit liability for Redwood.

2) Invoice treatment: we can do invoice-line credits across the first two invoices (conversion credit split 60/40) and still book ARR at contract value, with clear disclosure in SOW on recognition mechanics. This matches their procurement requirement and keeps finance clean.

3) Burst capacity: Marissa recommends adding a contracted burst buffer of 1 hot GPU (billed at a lower standby rate) available for 30-minute windows, with usage-based billing if exceeded. That meets the 2x short spikes without over-provisioning the whole commit.

4) SLA & measurement: propose 30-day rolling windows, exclude customer traffic patterns that exceed documented burst config, and include a 15-day remediation window before credits apply.

Action items: Neha — incorporate these into a clean two-option rate sheet and SOW language and push to Samantha. Priyom — I'll draft the legal bullet points for the SLA exclusions and the invoice credit wording. Marissa — please attach a short note about expected throughput headroom with the recommended burst buffer.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
rishi...@redwood.com
